uncited: It serves as the foundation for methods like [ZFP Block-Based Compression](1504-zfp-block-based-compression.md), [TSDF Block Transform Coding](2548-tsdf-block-transform-coding.md), [JPEG2000](2883-jpeg2000.md), and [Learned Transform Coding](7046-learned-transform-coding.md).
JPEG2000 is a wavelet-based compression standard for still images that serves as the primary benchmark for 2-D coding systems in volumetric data compression.
In volume rendering, it is used as a baseline where each 2D layer of a layered image is coded separately using JPEG2000 Part-1, referred to as "Individual layer coding".

This approach sets itself apart from 3D volumetric schemes by processing slices independently, which ignores inter-slice correlations and results in visible artifacts at layer boundaries compared to methods that exploit 3D redundancy.
